create.name: Nubia Teixeira
create.bio:
Nubia Teixeira is a Brazilian-born yoga teacher, Odissi dancer and author who started practising and teaching yoga in Brazil in her teens and has taught for more than thirty-five years. She came to California in 2001, where she continued her training in Odissi, the devotional classical dance of eastern India, with Sri Vishnu Tattva Das, having first studied it in São Paulo and in India. Her approach places the goddess at the centre of yoga practice, drawing on Shakta philosophy, bhakti devotion, Hatha Yoga and the expressive hand gestures of Indian dance.

She calls this work Mother Goddess Yoga: postures held long enough to build strength, combined with breath, mantra, prayer, poetry, story, mudra and imagery from nature, open to all bodies and genders. Her book Yoga and the Art of Mudras pairs yoga poses with symbolic gestures from the dance tradition, and she is writing a second book on Mother Goddess Yoga. Students can practise with her online through a Patreon community with circles, weekly classes, immersions and mentoring, or in person at retreats such as her annual immersion at the Omega Institute. She also trains yoga teachers, recorded a pranayama course with Sounds True, and often teaches alongside her husband, the kirtan musician Jai Uttal.

courses.title: Mother Goddess Yoga Online (Patreon)
courses.description: Nubia's online membership, with tiers ranging from a monthly circle to weekly practice, a twice-weekly immersion and personal mentoring. Classes blend postures, breath, mantra, mudra and goddess imagery.

courses.title: Mother Goddess Yoga Immersion at Omega Institute
courses.description: A five-day residential workshop at Omega in Rhinebeck, New York, teaching a goddess-centred yoga practice through postures, pranayama, mantra, mudra and visualisation. It is open to all ages and body types, with no prior yoga experience needed.

free_resources.title: Mudras in Yoga
free_resources.description: An extract from her book, published free on her blog, explaining what mudras are and how they are thought to direct subtle energy in practice.

free_resources.title: What is Bhakti Yoga?
free_resources.description: A free blog extract from her book introducing bhakti, the yoga of devotion, and how it shapes everyday life and service.
